body:
Targeted `checklist-test` run of the five approvals items PR #27112 rewrote (wave anchor #25807, slice C run). Every step was driven live, in a browser and over the API, on a fresh showcase boot. No clause was read from source alone.

Runner: cloud session `session_01QSeKYpK8js3AA3SHa3SyJH`, dispatched by seat `domain:devx#2` (claim 6462738260). The run was sequential, one runner and no subagents.

## Environment fingerprint

- Framework sha: `07d18e692` (current `origin/main` at boot). The console was built from `ui/` in the same tree with `pnpm build --concurrency=2` (116/116 tasks, 0 cached), then `pnpm console:build --concurrency=2`. `check-dev-prereqs` exit 0.
- Boot: `OS_PORT=41807 OS_STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT=/tmp/qa-25807/uploads pnpm -C examples/app-showcase exec objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p 41807 -d file:/tmp/qa-25807/data.db`, started under `setsid` and stopped through its own process group. The banner read `32 flow(s) 19 bound`, and scheduled work was off (the default).
- Seed: the stock showcase plus `--seed-admin`. The personas were the dev admin (org owner), Mei Phone (`usr_showcase_phone_demo`) and Ada Auditor (`usr_showcase_auditor_demo`), the last two with the password `showcase123`.
- Browser: Playwright chromium, headless, one context per persona, absolute origin `http://localhost:41807`.
- Clock: the run went from 2026-10-28T07:15Z (boot) to 07:33Z (teardown).

## Scope

The selector was `area:approvals` filtered to five ids. `node scripts/checklist-select.mjs ID --json` pinned these revisions:

| item | priority | surface | revision |
|---|---|---|---|
| approvals.viewer-gating-submitter-side | P1 | browser | 7 |
| approvals.notification-deep-link | P2 | browser | 8 |
| approvals.dynamic-approver-routing | P2 | mixed | 4 |
| approvals.inbox-keyboard-flow | P2 | browser | 3 |
| approvals.approver-resolution-matrix | P1 | api | 9 |

None of the five carries `automated.ref`, so every clause was driven by hand (tier 2). The selection contains no planned items.

## Per-clause verdicts

### approvals.viewer-gating-submitter-side (r7) — PASS

| clause | verdict | oracle evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 0 decision panel omits approver levers, keeps Send reminder / Recall | pass | Signed in as Mei through the form. Account app → Approvals → `/_console/apps/com.objectstack.account/component/approvals/inbox`; the "Submitted by me" tab listed EXP-2001 and EXP-DEMO. Clicking the EXP-2001 row navigated to `/apps/com.objectstack.account/sys_approval_request/record/areq_b860b571-…`. The screenshot shows the decision panel rendering exactly `Send reminder`, `Recall` and `Reply`, with no Approve, Reject, Reassign, Send back or Request info. The overflow menu holds only `Add to favorites / Open in new tab / Copy link`. |
| 1 viewer flags say why | pass | Mei called `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/areq_b860b571-…` and got 200: `viewer: {can_act:false, is_submitter:true, can_override:false}`, `pending_approvers: [admin, usr_showcase_auditor_demo]`, which does not contain her id. |
| 2 forged decision rejected; entitled side succeeds | pass | Mei's `POST …/approve {comment}` answered 403 `FORBIDDEN` "actor 'usr_showcase_phone_demo' is not a pending approver". With `actor_id: usr_showcase_auditor_demo` it answered 403 `FORBIDDEN` "cannot act as … recorded against the authenticated caller". On the entitled side, Ada's `POST …/approve` answered 200, and the actions list gained `approve · usr_showcase_auditor_demo`. |
| 3 forged call left no trace | pass | Admin reads of the request and of `/actions` before and after both forged calls were byte-identical (`true`/`true`). The only action row was `submit`. |

### approvals.notification-deep-link (r8) — PASS

Both landed on `/_console/apps/com.objectstack.setup/sys_approval_request/record/areq_a4b0b338-…` with `history.length` 2, so the deep link was replaced. Both drew "Announcement Dynamic Approval", step Lead Review, status Pending. |
| 2 page = API for that id | pass | `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/areq_a4b0b338-…` answered `process_label` "Announcement Dynamic Approval", `status` pending, `current_step_label` "Lead Review" and `pending_approver_names` {admin: "Dev Admin"}. The page showed the same title, status, step and Waiting on: Dev Admin. |
| 3 both routes land | pass | `/_console/apps/com.objectstack.account/component/approvals/inbox?request=areq_a4b0b338-…` landed on `/_console/apps/com.objectstack.account/sys_approval_request/record/areq_a4b0b338-…` and drew the same request. The `/system/approvals` route is covered in clause 1. |
| 4 unknown id → not-found, never another request | pass | `/_console/system/approvals?request=areq_does-not-exist-qa25807` landed on `/apps/com.objectstack.setup/sys_approval_request/record/areq_does-not-exist-qa25807`. The screenshot shows "Record not found — The record you are looking for does not exist or may have been deleted.", with no request content. The API answers 404 `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` for that id. |

### approvals.dynamic-approver-routing (r4) — PASS

| clause | verdict | oracle evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 0 typed sys_user multi-select | pass | On the request page, Approve opened a dialog. Its `Next Reviewers *` field is a `Select…` record-picker button, not a text input. The popover lists sys_user rows (Dev Admin, Ada Auditor (demo), Mei Phone (demo)) with a search box. Picking two showed `2 selected` with both chips. |
| 1 outputless approve refused, request stays pending | pass | `POST …/areq_a4b0b338-…/approve {comment}` answered 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` "decision output(s) `next_reviewers` are required to approve this request". The same with `outputs.next_reviewers: []` also answered 400. In the UI, Confirm with no pick posted nothing and showed "Next Reviewers is required". A re-read showed status pending, actions `[submit]` only. |
| 2 stage 2 resolves exactly the picked users | pass | The dialog's POST body was `{"outputs":{"next_reviewers":["admin"]}}`. The stage-2 request `areq_4c16dd92-…` (step `co_sign`) has `pending_approvers` [admin]. |
| 3 N picks → N approvers, in order | pass | A second chain on announcement `kjc0_5pFsdzYXfOz` posted `{"outputs":{"next_reviewers":["usr_showcase_auditor_demo","admin"]}}`. The stage-2 request `areq_f60cafa8-…` has `pending_approvers` [usr_showcase_auditor_demo, admin]: 1→1 and 2→2, in the picked order. |
| 4 deciding stage 2 completes the run | pass | Run `run_c62dbb36-…` went from paused to completed after the admin approved `areq_4c16dd92-…`. Run `run_66508f9b-…` stayed paused after Ada's approval (unanimous, admin still pending) and went to completed after the admin's. |

### approvals.inbox-keyboard-flow (r3) — PASS

| clause | verdict | oracle evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 0 j/k/arrows move a clamped ring; Enter opens the focused row | pass | The admin opened the inbox via the account app's Approvals entry, and the hint bar reads "Keyboard: j/k move · Enter open · x select · a approve · r reject". The screenshot confirmed the list of four rows. The ring (`ring-2` row class) moved j→0, j→1, k→0, ArrowDown→1, ArrowUp→0. It clamped: k at 0 stayed 0, and j past the end stayed at 3. Enter on row 1 (EXP-2001) landed on `…/sys_approval_request/record/areq_b860b571-…`, whose API read is `record_title` EXP-2001. |
| 1 a/r use the same dialog and the same server transition | pass | r on EXP-DEMO opened an alertdialog, "Reject "EXP-DEMO"? … Cancel Reject", with zero POSTs before the confirm. Confirming sent exactly one `POST /api/v1/approvals/requests/areq_11e24c06-…/reject {"actor_id":"admin"}` → 200; the re-read showed status rejected and actions [submit, reject]. a on INV-1008 sent one `POST …/areq_80e02596-…/approve {"actor_id":"admin"}` → 200, approved. The row's own Approve button (EXP-2001) produced the same dialog shape and the same route and body, `{"actor_id":"admin"}`, with actions going 2→3. The My Pending badge went 4→3→2. |
| 2 keyboard ownership guards | pass | Input guard: a keydown dispatched on the focused search input for each of j, k, a, r and Enter left the ring at [1], opened no dialog, did not navigate and sent no POST. A positive control, the same synthetic keydown on body, moved the ring 1→2→1. Real typing into the input is confounded by the list filter (focus is clamped when the filter empties the list), which is why the synthetic leg exists. Dialog guard: with the reject alertdialog open, j left the ring unchanged and sent no POST. Enter was not pressed inside the dialog, because focus sits on its own Cancel button and Enter would activate that button natively. On this page the decide dialog and the alertdialog are one element, so those two guards are exercised together. |
| 3 a/r gated by quick-decidability | pass | On the dynamic-approval stage-1 row (declared `next_reviewers`), a and r opened no dialog and sent no POST. The row's buttons are replaced by "This approval collects decision outputs — open it to decide." |
| 4 x/space select only on the pending tab | pass | On My Pending, x on row 1 put it in the selected set and the bulk bar read "1 selected"; space toggled it off again. On "Submitted by me", x selected nothing, and that tab renders no row checkboxes. |

### approvals.approver-resolution-matrix (r9) — PASS

The provisioning ran as the admin:

- BU memberships: Ada in `bu_field_ops` (parent) and Mei in `bu_east_coast` (a child of `bu_field_ops`), via `POST /api/v1/data/sys_business_unit_member` → 201.
- Team `CbEbrsrhMgxvyLo5vEBR8Ci3GCfSbczO` holding Ada and Mei, via `create-team` / `add-team-member` → 200.
- Manager: Mei → Ada, via `set-user-manager` → 200.
- Queue `qa_matrix_queue` with Ada and Mei as members, and `qa_empty_queue` with none, via `sys_queue` / `sys_queue_member` → 201.

Each leg registered a scratch active flow through `POST /api/v1/automation` (200), triggered it by a `showcase_field_zoo` create, read the requests, and deregistered the flow with `DELETE /api/v1/automation/NAME` (200).

| clause | verdict | oracle evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 0 per-variant slates | pass | user `usr_showcase_auditor_demo` → [Ada]. field `f_users` = [Mei, Ada] → [Mei, Ada]. manager over `f_user` = Mei → [Ada]. team → [Ada, Mei]. department `bu_field_ops` → [Mei, Ada]. queue → [Ada, Mei]. org_membership_level `owner` → [admin], the only `sys_member` row with role owner. role `owner` → [admin]. expression: see dynamic-approver-routing clauses 2–3 of this run. position: the seeded `INV-1008` (finance ∧ legal) opened on [admin, admin], whose `sys_user_position` rows hold finance and legal. |
| 1 department walks active descendants | pass | The parent-unit slate was [Mei (descendant `bu_east_coast`), Ada (parent)]. After `PATCH sys_business_unit/bu_east_coast {active:false}` and a re-trigger, the slate was [Ada]. The unit was re-activated afterwards. |
| 2 field fans out per id | pass | `pending_approvers` was two entries, `__resolvedFrom` `{"field:f_users":[Mei, Ada]}`, and no CSV literal appeared. |
| 3 role warns and resolves identically | pass | The log line reads `WARN [approvals] approver type 'role' is deprecated (ADR-0090 D3) — author 'org_membership_level' instead {"deprecated":"role","canonical":"org_membership_level"}`. The registration advisory `approval-approver-type-deprecated` also fired. The slates were equal: role [admin] and org_membership_level [admin]. |
| 4 empty-slate forks | pass | **admin_rescue** (default, unstaffed `position:qa_unstaffed_pos`): pending, `pending_approvers` [admin] (the organization's only administrator, `sys_member` role owner), `__resolvedFrom` `{"admin_rescue:abandoned":["position:qa_unstaffed_pos"],"admin_rescue:reason":"position 'qa_unstaffed_pos' has no holder"}`. The action is a system comment (no actor), "Routed to this organization's administrators because the approver slate named no one: position 'qa_unstaffed_pos' has no holder.", and the WARN reads "… opening on this organization's administrators per onEmptyApprovers: 'admin_rescue'". **fail**: no request row; the run failed with `NO_APPROVERS: approval node 'appr' … onEmptyApprovers policy is 'fail'`. **auto_approve**: no request row; the run completed with steps `start, appr, mark` all success, the approve-edge marker wrote `f_textarea = qa-approve-edge-marker`, and the WARN reads "auto-approving per onEmptyApprovers: 'auto_approve' (no request opened)". **fallback** (`{type:'user', value: Ada}`): opened on [Ada] with no literal slot, and the WARN reads "opening on the declared fallbackApprovers". **fallback resolving to nobody** (another unstaffed position): the WARN reads "AND its declared fallbackApprovers resolved to nobody either — falling back to admin_rescue". It opened on [admin] with reason "…; the declared fallbackApprovers resolved to no one either". |
| 5 queue routes to members; empty queue is loud | pass | Staffed: `pending_approvers` [Ada, Mei], which equals the planted `sys_queue_member` rows, with no `queue:` entry. Empty (`qa_empty_queue`) and no-row (`qa_no_such_queue`): the WARN reads "approver 'queue:qa_empty_queue' expanded to nobody — the queue has no members in this organization … It adds no slot to this request". The request stayed pending on [admin], with `__resolvedFrom` `{"admin_rescue:abandoned":[],"admin_rescue:reason":"no approver on the node resolved to a person"}` (read on the data door) and the routed-to-administrators comment in its actions. |

The negatives held throughout. Every graph expansion to nobody carried the "expanded to nobody" WARN naming type and value: `department:bu_hq_finance` beside a staffed user, `position:qa_unstaffed_pos(2)`, `queue:*`. No empty slate finalized under admin_rescue, and no admin_rescue request opened on a literal slot alone.

## Off-clause probes (RUNNER rule 8)

These took about 3 minutes on the same boot, as Mei, Ada and the admin.

- Boundary ids: an unknown id answered 404 `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` for both read and approve.
- Opposite posture: Mei's forged reject answered 403, her reassign on a request she is not on answered 403, and her remind on a request she did not submit answered 403. Her read of a request she is neither on nor submitted answered 404 (not disclosed).
- List door: an unknown param answered 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`. An empty `?status=` answered 200 with the unfiltered list. That is an observation, not filed: an empty value reads as absent there, while `limit`/`offset` refuse empty.
- Recipient scope: every `sys_inbox_message` row visible to Mei and to Ada is addressed to that persona. Each was notified only for requests whose slate names them.

None of this found a filable defect.
